units.title: 3.1 The nature of law and the English legal system

outcomes.text: Study the nature of law and the English legal system.
Distinguish enforceable legal rules from other rules and norms of behaviour.
Distinguish criminal from civil law and the sources: custom, statute and common law.
Explain the role of law in society and the balance between competing public and private interests.
Explain the meaning and importance of fault in civil and criminal law.
Distinguish law from morality in a society with varied moral views.
Explain the relationship between law and morality and legal enforcement of moral values.
Explain the meaning of justice and theories of justice.
Judge how far civil and criminal law achieve justice.
Explain the rule of law: sanction only under law, equality before law, fairness and clarity.
Explain Green and White papers and the formal legislative process.
Explain influences on Parliament and the advantages and disadvantages of each.
Explain parliamentary supremacy and its limits.
Name the types: orders in council, statutory instruments, bylaws.
Explain parliamentary and judicial controls on delegated legislation.
Explain the reasons for it and its advantages and disadvantages.
Apply the literal, golden and mischief rules and the purposive approach.
Use internal and external aids to interpretation.
Explain how EU law and the Human Rights Act 1998 affect interpretation.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of each approach.
Explain the doctrine of judicial precedent and the court hierarchy including the Supreme Court.
Explain stare decisis, ratio decidendi, obiter dicta and law reporting.
Explain following, overruling and distinguishing.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of precedent.

subtopics.title: Law reform and the European Union

outcomes.text: Describe the Law Commission's work: reform, codification, consolidation and repeal.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of Law Commission reform.
Describe the EU Council, Commission, Parliament and Court of Justice and their functions.
Distinguish EU treaties, regulations and directives and their impact on English law.
Describe the civil courts, the track system and appeals.
Describe tribunals, mediation and negotiation.
Describe the criminal process, classification of offences and appeals.
Describe criminal court powers and sentencing of adults.
Explain the role and powers of magistrates and juries.
Weigh the advantages and disadvantages of juries.
Distinguish the roles of barristers, solicitors and legal executives and how they are regulated.
Describe types of judge and judges' roles in civil and criminal courts.
Explain judicial independence: security of tenure, immunity from suit, independence from the Executive.
Explain why judicial independence matters and how it is achieved.
Describe alternative sources of legal advice: help lines, CAB, law centres, trade unions.
Describe private funding: own resources, insurance, conditional fee agreements.
Describe public funding in criminal and civil cases.
Study the rules of criminal law: general liability, offences against the person, property and attempt.
Explain harm as the basis for criminalising conduct.
Explain autonomy, fault and individual responsibility.
Explain fair labelling, correspondence, maximum certainty and no retrospective liability.
Explain actus reus: conduct, omissions, state of affairs, voluntariness, causation and consequences.
Explain mens rea: intention, subjective recklessness, negligence and transferred malice.
Explain strict liability and the coincidence of actus reus and mens rea.
Explain murder.
Explain voluntary manslaughter: loss of control and diminished responsibility.
Explain involuntary manslaughter: unlawful act and gross negligence.
Explain common assault and battery.
Explain s47, s20 and s18 Offences Against the Person Act 1861.
Explain theft and robbery.
Explain attempt under the Criminal Attempts Act 1981.
Apply the capacity defences: insanity, automatism and intoxication.
Apply self-defence and prevention of crime.
Apply necessity defences: duress and duress of circumstances.

subtopics.title: Tort principles and duty of care

outcomes.text: Study liability and fault in negligence, occupiers' liability, nuisance and vicarious liability, with defences and remedies.
Explain the public policy behind the duty of care, using the Caparo test.
Explain the 'neighbour' principle and the duty of care in physical injury and property damage.
Explain breach of duty and the objective standard of care.
Explain damage: factual causation and legal causation (remoteness).
Explain liability for pure economic loss from negligent acts and misstatements.
Explain liability for psychiatric injury to primary and secondary victims.
Explain liability to visitors under the Occupiers' Liability Act 1957.
Explain liability to trespassers under the Occupiers' Liability Act 1984.
Explain private nuisance.
Explain the rule in Rylands v Fletcher.
Explain the nature and purpose of vicarious liability.
Test employment status.
Explain other areas of vicarious liability.
Apply contributory negligence and consent (volenti).
Apply defences specific to private nuisance and Rylands v Fletcher.
Explain compensatory damages and mitigation of loss.
Explain injunctions and how conflicting interests are balanced.
Study formation, terms, vitiating factors, discharge and remedies of contract.
Explain freedom of contract and the need to protect consumers.
Distinguish offers, unilateral offers and invitations to treat.
Explain acceptance, the postal rule and electronic communications.
Explain consideration, privity, and links to economic duress.
Explain intention to create legal relations.
Distinguish express from implied terms.
Distinguish conditions, warranties and innominate terms.
Apply terms implied in goods contracts: satisfactory quality, fitness for purpose, description (s9-s11).
Apply goods remedies: short-term right to reject, repair or replacement, price reduction (s20, s23, s24).
Apply terms implied in service contracts: reasonable care and skill, reasonable time (s49, s52).
Apply service remedies: repeat performance, price reduction (s55, s56).
Explain exclusion and limitation clauses and their effectiveness.
Explain common law control: incorporation and construction.
Explain statutory control: Unfair Contract Terms Act 1977 and Consumer Rights Act 2015.
Explain misrepresentation: nature, types and remedies.
Explain economic duress: definition and remedies.
Explain discharge by performance, breach (actual and anticipatory) and frustration.
Explain compensatory damages: loss categories, causation, remoteness and mitigation.
Explain specific performance and rescission.
Explain termination for breach.
Study rights to life, liberty, privacy, expression, and assembly and association.
Explain theories of rights.
Contrast rights with liberties.
Explain the scope of fundamental human rights.
Explain the Second World War and its aftermath.
Explain the UN and the Universal Declaration of Human Rights 1948.
Explain the Council of Europe and the European Convention on Human Rights 1953.
Explain the Convention's UK status before the Human Rights Act and the impact of the European Court's decisions.
Explain how the Convention was incorporated and interpreted by the Act.
Explain impact on constitutional arrangements and the Act's entrenchment in devolution.
Evaluate criticisms of human rights.

topics.title: The European Convention on Human Rights

outcomes.text: Explain Article 2: right to life and justified exceptions.
Explain Article 5: right to liberty and security, lawful arrest or detention, and extra requirements.
Explain Article 8: respect for private and family life, home and correspondence.
Explain Article 10: freedom of expression.
Explain Article 11: peaceful assembly and association.
Explain restrictions under Articles 8.2, 10.2 and 11.2 and the general requirements for them.
Explain claims before the European Court of Human Rights and the role of domestic courts.
Explain the effect of decisions on states and claimants.
Explain judicial review.
Outline criminal and civil protection of the right to life, including homicide, policing duties, negligence and investigations.
Outline law on deprivation of liberty.
Outline law protecting or restricting privacy and communication.
Balance privacy against expression, assembly and association.
Discuss reform of human rights protection in the UK.
